title: Cohomological bounds for derived extension of ring-sheaf scalars
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], and let $R\to S$ be a morphism of sheaves of commutative rings on $\mathcal C$. Use the abelian categories of sheaves of modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], their unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and the standard cohomological bounds [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category]. Write $F(M)=M\otimes_R^LS$ for derived extension of scalars, computed using K-flat resolutions [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. For a sheaf of $R$-modules $N$ and $p>0$ define the sheaf $\operatorname{Tor}_p^R(N,S)=\mathcal H^{-p}(N[0]\otimes_R^LS)$.

For every $a\in\mathbf Z$:

(a) If $M\in D(\operatorname{Mod}(R))$ has $\mathcal H^i(M)=0$ for $i>a$, then $\mathcal H^i(F(M))=0$ for $i>a$.

(b) If $M\in D(\operatorname{Mod}(R))$ has $\mathcal H^i(M)=0$ for $i<a$, and $\operatorname{Tor}_p^R(\mathcal H^q(M),S)=0$ for every $q\ge a$ and $p>0$, then $\mathcal H^i(F(M))=0$ for $i<a$.

No upper cohomological bound is assumed in (b), and no boundedness, finite generation, flatness of $S$ over $R$, or existence of points of the site is assumed beyond the hypotheses just stated.

source.place: Tag 06YU (definition-derived-tor), for derived sheaf tensor; Tag 077J (lemma-resolution-by-direct-sums-extensions-by-zero), for compatible bounded-above flat resolutions of upper truncations, lines 3168-3197. proof.text: Prove (a). By [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category], choose a representative $G$ of $M$ with $G^i=0$ for $i>a$ (equivalently take the good upper truncation of any representative). Apply [lem-pc-kflat-bounded-flat-replacement] with $\mathcal O=R$ and $N=a$ to obtain a quasi-isomorphism $P\to G$ with flat terms and $P^i=0$ for $i>a$. The site version [lem-pc-bounded-above-flat-kflat-site] makes $P$ K-flat. By [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], $F(M)$ is represented by the termwise tensor complex $P\otimes_RS$. Its terms above $a$ are zero, hence so are its cohomology sheaves above $a$. This proves (a) with no lower bound.

source.place: Tags 06YQ (lemma-bounded-flat-K-flat), 06YU (definition-derived-tor); bounded-above replacement used in Tag 077J (lemma-resolution-by-direct-sums-extensions-by-zero).

proof.text: Record the degree-zero case needed for (b). If $N$ is an $R$-module sheaf with $\operatorname{Tor}_p^R(N,S)=0$ for $p>0$, the definition of Tor in the item gives $\mathcal H^i(F(N[0]))=0$ for $i<0$ by putting $p=-i$. Step 1 applied with upper bound zero gives vanishing for $i>0$. Since [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] is an exact functor of triangulated categories, it commutes with shifts; thus $F(N[-q])\simeq F(N[0])[-q]$ has cohomology only in degree $q$. The sign convention $(X[-q])^i=X^{i-q}$ is that of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. No identification of the remaining degree-zero sheaf is needed.

source.place: Tag 06YU (definition-derived-tor), the subsequent definition-tor and cohomological shift convention.

proof.text:
First prove the lower bound for finite upper truncations, with a finite induction explicitly starting below $a$. Let $M$ satisfy (b), and put $M_{\le b}=\tau_{\le b}M$. If $b<a$, this object is zero: its cohomology vanishes in every degree, so the map from the zero complex to a representing complex is a quasi-isomorphism and becomes invertible in the derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. For $b\ge a$, induct from $b=a-1$ using the successive-truncation triangle of [lem-weil-pbc-truncation-triangle],
$$M_{\le b-1}\longrightarrow M_{\le b}\longrightarrow\mathcal H^b(M)[-b]\longrightarrow M_{\le b-1}[1].$$
Apply the exact functor of [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. The left term after applying $F$ has no cohomology below $a$ by the induction hypothesis, and the right term has cohomology only in degree $b\ge a$ by Step 2 and the Tor hypothesis. For $i<a$ the exact segment $\mathcal H^i(F(M_{\le b-1}))\to\mathcal H^i(F(M_{\le b}))\to\mathcal H^i(F(\mathcal H^b(M)[-b]))$ from [lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact] has zero outer objects, so its middle object is zero. This proves $F(M_{\le b})\in D^{\ge a}$ for every finite integer $b$.

Choose any cochain representative $G$ of $M$. Apply [lem-pc-flat-truncation-tower] to get bounded-above termwise flat complexes $E_n$, transitions $t_n$, and quasi-isomorphisms $q_n:E_n\to\tau_{\le n}G$ for $n\in\mathbf N$. Set $e_n=\iota_n\circ q_n:E_n\to G$. The compatibility in that node, written as the map equality $\iota_{n+1}\circ q_{n+1}\circ t_n=\iota_n\circ q_n$, says exactly $e_{n+1}\circ t_n=e_n$. Hence these maps induce $e:P=\varinjlim_nE_n\to G$ on the degreewise sheaf colimit. By [lem-pc-module-filtered-colimits-tensor], filtered colimits of $R$-module sheaves are exact. Consequently they commute with cohomology: exactness preserves kernels of the differentials and images of the previous differentials, and preserves the quotient of those two objects in the formula of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. For each fixed $i$, $H^i(e_n)$ is an isomorphism for every $n\ge\max(0,i)$, because $q_n$ is a quasi-isomorphism and the good truncation inclusion retains cohomology through degree $n$. The compatibility of the $e_n$ identifies all transitions on this tail with the identity of $H^i(G)$. Thus $H^i(e):\varinjlim_nH^i(E_n)\to H^i(G)$ is an isomorphism. Therefore $e$ is a quasi-isomorphism. This uses a degreewise colimit of complexes, without assuming a colimit calculation in a derived category.

source.place: Tag 077J (lemma-resolution-by-direct-sums-extensions-by-zero), compatible resolutions and their colimit; Tag 03DB (lemma-limits-colimits), exact filtered colimits.

proof.text: The complex $P$ of Step 4 is K-flat. Each $E_n$ is K-flat by [lem-pc-bounded-above-flat-kflat-site]. For any acyclic $R$-module complex $A$, [lem-pc-module-filtered-colimits-tensor] identifies $P\otimes_RA$ with $\varinjlim_n(E_n\otimes_RA)$. The signed symmetry $x\otimes y\mapsto(-1)^{rs}y\otimes x$, for $x$ of degree $r$ and $y$ of degree $s$, identifies the order here with that in [def-pc-kflat-complex]; substituting into the differential $d(x\otimes y)=dx\otimes y+(-1)^r x\otimes dy$ of [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves] verifies the chain-map identity, and applying the symmetry twice gives the identity. Hence each $E_n\otimes_RA$ is acyclic. Exact filtered colimits commute with cohomology by the kernel-image-quotient calculation of Step 4, so $P\otimes_RA$ is acyclic, and symmetry gives the same for $A\otimes_RP$. This is precisely K-flatness. Together with $e:P\to G$, it supplies a K-flat resolution of $M$.

source.place: Tag 06YR (lemma-colimit-K-flat), with the tensor-colimit calculation of Tag 03EP (lemma-tensor-commute-colimits).

proof.text:
Compute $F(M)$ by this K-flat resolution using [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. Its representing complex is $P\otimes_RS$, whose underlying $R$-module complex is $\varinjlim_n(E_n\otimes_RS)$ by [lem-pc-module-filtered-colimits-tensor] with fixed second factor $S[0]$. Each $E_n$ is K-flat and represents $\tau_{\le n}M$, so the same change-of-rings node identifies $E_n\otimes_RS$ with $F(\tau_{\le n}M)$. Step 3 therefore gives $H^i(E_n\otimes_RS)=0$ for every $n$ and every $i<a$, including $n<a$. Applying the exact-colimit cohomology calculation from Step 4 gives
$$H^i(P\otimes_RS)=\varinjlim_nH^i(E_n\otimes_RS)=0\qquad(i<a).$$
These calculations may be made after restricting the $S$-module structure to $R$: kernels consist of the same sections killed by the differential and cokernels are the same sheafified quotient groups, with the inherited scalar action [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Thus vanishing as an $R$-module sheaf is vanishing as an $S$-module sheaf. This proves (b), with no upper bound on $M$ and without using points of the site.

lean.statement: theorem ringedTensorCohomologicalBounds {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] [EssentiallySmall.{r} C] {J : GrothendieckTopology C} [J.HasSheafCompose (forget₂ CommRingCat.{r} RingCat.{r})] [J.WEqualsLocallyBijective AddCommGrpCat.{r}] [HasSheafify J AddCommGrpCat.{r}] {R S : Sheaf J CommRingCat.{r}} (φ : R ⟶ S) [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{r} (derivedChangeRingIndependentCoefficients J R))] [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{r} (derivedChangeRingIndependentCoefficients J S))] (a : ℤ) : (∀ M : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{r} (derivedChangeRingIndependentCoefficients J R)), M.IsLE a → ((ringedDerivedScalarExtension φ).obj M).IsLE a) ∧ (∀ M : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{r} (derivedChangeRingIndependentCoefficients J R)), M.IsGE a → (∀ (q : ℤ), a ≤ q → ∀ (p : ℕ), 0 < p → IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (SheafOfModules.{r} (derivedChangeRingIndependentCoefficients J S)) (-(p : ℤ))).obj ((ringedDerivedScalarExtension φ).obj (DerivedCategory.Q.obj ((CochainComplex.singleFunctor (SheafOfModules.{r} (derivedChangeRingIndependentCoefficients J R)) 0).obj ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (SheafOfModules.{r} (derivedChangeRingIndependentCoefficients J R)) q).obj M)))))) → ((ringedDerivedScalarExtension φ).obj M).IsGE a)
